teaser.text: Mastercard is a payments company that connects institutions so money can move between them. It earns fees from that connection and from services built around it, while other institutions usually lend, hold and transfer the purchase money.

stock.opening: Mastercard's weighted forecast reaches US$718.71 in October 2029, with the base case at 55% probability, the bear case at 25% and the bull case at 20%. It hinges on whether network growth and paid services keep outrunning incentives, routing pressure and BVNK's costs.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains Mastercard's business, its rivals, its management and its risks.

blocks.heading: Where could Mastercard's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted forecast is US$628.65 in October 2027, implying a 10% total return. It reaches US$718.71 in October 2029, implying a 27% total return. The final-date cases span US$421.58 to US$1,106.97. The base case has 55% probability. The bear case has 25%; the bull case has 20%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Mastercard?

paragraphs.text: The base P/E falls from 29x to 27x and then 25x. That starts above the current 24.9x forward P/E but moves toward Visa’s 26.0x as growth normalizes. The bear path falls from 23x to 20x and then 18x because incentives, routing pressure and legal uncertainty reduce confidence. The bull path rises from 33x to 34x and then 35x, requiring sustained services growth and investor confidence. The full assumptions are shown below.

Weaker travel, alternative routing and the Capital One debit migration slow activity. Incentives continue to outpace GDV, while merchant and regulatory pressure weighs on pricing. Lower cash conversion reduces buybacks, and investors assign a lower multiple. The path reaches $461.09 in the first year and $421.58 in the last, including dividends. Its probability is 25% because the operating and valuation risks are visible, although rising historical net income makes sustained deterioration less likely.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Mastercard really make?

paragraphs.text: Software changes the picture. Mastercard spent $726 million on capitalized software, separately from property and equipment. After deducting that spending, free cash flow was $16,433 million; after also deducting stock-based pay, it was $15,836 million. Stock compensation is not a cash payment today, but shareholders bear dilution or the cost of repurchasing shares to offset it.
The durable measure is cash left after software, customer acquisition and dilution—not merely cash left after property spending.

dividend.title: Mastercard dividend: cash coverage
dividend.meta_description: Mastercard pays a growing dividend from strong cash generation, while incentives, routing pressure and cash needs could change its path.
dividend.opening: Mastercard's latest quarterly dividend is $0.87 per share, and forecast dividends per share rise from $3.84 to $4.80. Mastercard's real free cash flow after stock pay totalled $60,732 million across the period; dividends used $11,006 million and buybacks used $46,370 million.
dividend.closing: The full Mastercard memo also explains its business, rivals, management outlook and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Mastercard pay per share?

paragraphs.text: Base dividends per share rise from $3.84 to $4.29 and then $4.80. This implies growth below the historical pace, but still fits the latest $0.87 quarterly dividend and an approximately 18–19% payout. The bear path reaches $3.60, $3.79 and $3.99 as cash competes with debt, investment and buybacks. The bull path reaches $3.92, $4.50 and $5.18 if earnings and cash growth support increases near the historical rate.

blocks.heading: Does Mastercard's cash cover its dividend?

paragraphs.text: Across the period, real free cash flow after stock pay totalled $60,732 million. Buybacks absorbed $46,370 million and dividends another $11,006 million. Together, they used about 94.5% of that cash. A dividend pays owners directly. A buyback pays shareholders who sell and reduces the number of shares remaining, giving continuing owners a larger fraction of the company.

paragraphs.text: The forecast would move toward the bear case in 2027–2028 if portfolio migration or alternative routing slowed GDV and switched transactions, or if incentives continued rising faster than activity.

blocks.heading: What is Mastercard's dividend yield today?

paragraphs.text: A 3.3% free cash flow yield means the business generates about $3.30 of annual cash for every $100 invested. The 0.6% dividend yield is the smaller portion paid directly as dividends. Buybacks can raise earnings per share, but debt-funded repurchases do not make the underlying business more productive.

earnings.title: Mastercard earnings: guidance and what to watch
earnings.meta_description: Mastercard expects October 29, 2026 results to test revenue growth, expense control and cash conversion.
earnings.opening: Mastercard's next results are expected on October 29, 2026. Watch whether profit becomes operating cash.
earnings.closing: The full Mastercard analysis also covers Mastercard’s business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: What has Mastercard guided for the year?

paragraphs.text: The clearest view of the ordinary business removes exchange-rate movements and acquisitions or disposals. On that currency-neutral, organic basis, Mastercard expects revenue growth at the high end of low double digits and operating-expense growth in the low double digits. Because revenue should grow faster, operating profit should grow faster than revenue.

Management kept the range unchanged but said stronger first-half results made it more confident about finishing at the higher end. The September quarter will test that confidence. Mastercard again expects underlying revenue growth at the high end of low double digits, against low double-digit expense growth.

blocks.heading: Has Mastercard kept its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Mastercard separately promised 2025–27 revenue growth at the high end of low double digits and EPS growth in the mid-teens. In 2025, currency-neutral adjusted revenue and EPS each grew 15%. That is a first year consistent with the direction of the promise, but the full period remains unfinished.

blocks.heading: What has Mastercard’s revenue and profit trend been?

paragraphs.text: Revenue rose 14.1% year over year, while operating income rose 17.0%. Net income increased 18.6%, and diluted EPS increased 22.1%. The operating margin reached 60.2%, up from 58.7%. The comparison with the same quarter a year earlier is more useful than the sequential comparison because payment activity and costs are seasonal.

blocks.heading: What should you watch in Mastercard’s next results?

paragraphs.text: The next results will show whether Mastercard’s stronger outlook becomes cash it can retain. The September-quarter results are expected to be published on October 29, 2026, though that is an analyst estimate of the date rather than a confirmed company announcement. Investors should watch whether revenue outgrows underlying expenses and whether profit becomes operating cash. BVNK’s first partial quarter may reveal integration costs, but not its eventual return.
